title: Load a class by its name

blocks.text: There are three ways to a `Class` object: `obj.getClass()`, a literal such as `String.class`, and `Class.forName(name)`. They all reach the **same** object. Only `forName` works from a string, so it is the one a plugin system or a config file uses.

items: `load(name, initialize)` loads the class with that name through `ClassLookup`'s own class loader. When `initialize` is `true` the class's **static initializer runs**; when it is `false` the class is **loaded but not initialized**. A name no class has gives **`Optional.empty()`** (`ClassNotFoundException` is checked: handle it).
`nameFor(type)` returns the name that `load` accepts back. For a nested class that is the **binary name** `Outer$Inner`, not the source-style `Outer.Inner`.

rows: the class, static block not run yet

cases.says: load("java.util.ArrayList", true) gives the same Class object as ArrayList.class and as getClass() on a list, and nameFor gives its name back.
A name no class has gives an empty Optional instead of an exception.
load(name, false) returns the class and its static initializer has not run.
load(name, true) runs the class's static initializer.
nameFor a nested class gives Outer$Inner, and load accepts it.

concepts: getName() gives the binary name Outer$Inner that forName accepts, where getCanonicalName() gives the source-style Outer.Inner.
Class.forName throws the checked ClassNotFoundException, which the caller must handle.
Class.forName(name) runs the static initializer, while forName(name, false, loader) loads the class without initializing it.
getClass(), a class literal and Class.forName all reach the one Class object of a type, and only forName works from a string.
